sections.markdown:
## C — Where passing is forbidden, how to drive a roundabout, how a diverging diamond interchange works, parking safely and lawfully, accessible parking, backing up, parallel parking and parking on a hill
Knowledge domain: the places a driver may never pass, the yield and lane rules of a roundabout, the crossover design of a diverging diamond interchange, the basic parking duty on a public road, who may use accessible spaces, and the step-by-step backing, parallel parking and hill parking techniques.

FACT_ID: sec07-F01 | anchor: A01
You may never pass on the right by leaving the paved or main part of the roadway. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F02 | anchor: A01
Passing is forbidden where your lane is bordered by a double solid line or by a solid dividing line on your side. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F03 | anchor: A01
Do not pass when approaching a curve or a hilltop where you cannot see far enough ahead to know passing is safe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F04 | anchor: A01
Do not pass within 100 feet of a street crossing or within 100 feet of a railroad crossing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F05 | anchor: A01
Do not pass within 100 feet of a bridge, tunnel or underpass that blocks your view. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F06 | anchor: A01
A roundabout is a circular intersection where traffic moves almost nonstop in one direction around a central island. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F07 | anchor: A01
At a roundabout, always yield to pedestrians and bicyclists who are crossing the road. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F08 | anchor: A01
Always enter a roundabout to the right of its central island. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F09 | anchor: A01
Drivers arriving at a roundabout must yield to every vehicle already circulating and to large vehicles entering at the same moment. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F10 | anchor: A01
Decide where you are going before you reach a roundabout, follow the signs and move into the right lane for your exit. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F11 | anchor: A01
Slow down on approach, because roundabouts are designed for speeds of 15 to 20 mph. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F12 | anchor: A01
Enter only when there is a gap, do not stop once you are inside, and follow signs or pavement markings for which lane to use. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F13 | anchor: A01
You may leave a roundabout at any street, and if you miss your exit you can simply go around again. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F14 | anchor: A01
Vehicles already in the roundabout have the right-of-way. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F15 | anchor: A01
Yield to large trucks entering a roundabout and do not try to pass them inside it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F16 | anchor: A01
If you see an emergency vehicle while in a roundabout, proceed carefully and exit if you can, or else pull over to the right. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F17 | anchor: A01
Pedestrians at roundabouts should use the crosswalks with caution, and bicyclists should either follow the traffic rules or walk the bike across in the crosswalks. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-F18 | anchor: A02
Coming up to a roundabout, slow down and yield until a safe gap opens, then enter and finish your turn or U-turn. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec07-F19 | anchor: A02
A diverging diamond interchange is a newer design now used at some Arizona freeway interchanges. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec07-F20 | anchor: A02
In a diverging diamond, traffic on the cross street above or below the freeway briefly moves over to the left side of the road to improve flow and safety. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec07-F21 | anchor: A02
You drive through a diverging diamond the same way as other interchanges, by following its traffic signals, signs and pavement markings. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec07-F22 | anchor: A02
The crossover points, where cross-street traffic moves from the right side to the left side of the road and back, happen at the signals. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec07-F23 | anchor: A02
Signals in a diverging diamond are simpler because no green-light time has to be set aside for left turns from the cross street onto the on-ramps. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec07-F24 | anchor: A02
In a diverging diamond, left turns onto the on-ramps are made from free-flowing lanes after the crossover. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec07-F25 | anchor: A02
When parking on a public road, make sure you are not blocking traffic, not blocking anyone's view and not in a zone where parking is illegal. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec07-F26 | anchor: A03
The international symbol of access, shown on reserved parking signs, placards and license plates, identifies parking for persons with disabilities. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec07-F27 | anchor: A03
A space marked with that symbol may be used only by a vehicle showing a valid placard or plate bearing it, and only while carrying the person the placard or plate was issued to. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec07-F28 | anchor: A03
Anyone else who parks in an accessible space is breaking the law and may be fined. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec07-F29 | anchor: A03
Backing up is dangerous because it is hard to see what is behind you. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec07-F30 | anchor: A03
Check behind the car before getting in, since children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec07-F31 | anchor: A03
To back up, turn around and look straight out the rear window rather than depending on mirrors or a backup camera. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec07-F32 | anchor: A03
Always back up slowly. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec07-F33 | anchor: A03
Keep checking for oncoming traffic while parallel parking; judging distance while controlling your speed is the key to the maneuver. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec07-F34 | anchor: A03
The first step of parallel parking is to check traffic behind you and signal that you are stopping. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec07-F35 | anchor: A03
Stop beside the forward car with your back bumper even with its back bumper, about two feet away from it. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec07-F36 | anchor: A03
Shift into reverse and, looking over your right shoulder, back slowly while turning the wheel sharply to the right. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec07-F37 | anchor: A03
Once your front bumper clears the forward car's rear bumper, turn the wheel sharply left and keep backing until you are parallel to the curb. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec07-F38 | anchor: A03
Finish parallel parking by straightening the wheels and pulling forward slowly. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec07-F39 | anchor: A03
Parked facing downhill with a curb, turn the front wheels toward the curb and set the parking brake. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec07-F40 | anchor: A03
Parked facing uphill with a curb, turn the wheels to the left and let the car roll back until the right front wheel rests against the curb, then set the parking brake. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec07-F41 | anchor: A03
Where there is no curb, point the wheels to the right, so a car whose brakes failed would roll away from the middle of the road. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec07-F42 | anchor: A03
Whatever the slope, always set the parking brake. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

Misconceptions: vehicles inside a roundabout have the right-of-way, not the vehicle that arrives first; you never stop inside a roundabout to wait, you keep moving and go around again if you miss your exit; backup cameras and mirrors do not replace turning around to look; uphill with a curb is the one case where the wheels point away from the curb.
Mnemonics: Downhill toward, uphill away, no curb to the right; in a roundabout, yield in and keep moving.
Glossary: roundabout means a circular intersection with one-way traffic around a central island; diverging diamond interchange means a freeway interchange where cross-street traffic briefly drives on the left side; crossover means the signalized point where traffic switches sides; international symbol of access means the wheelchair symbol marking accessible parking.
Dynamic facts: the manual says diverging diamonds are in use at some Arizona interchanges without listing them, so locations must come from ADOT; accessible-parking fines are not stated in the manual.
